requirements.reason: Pickup Lane needs PostgreSQL-backed durable job state with enforceable lifecycle, identity, lease, attempt, and safe metadata invariants before later WS05 consumers can use background work.
Durable work must be created transactionally and idempotently from local state without starting workers, providers, or duplicate side effects.
Independent PostgreSQL sessions must prove atomic claim, SKIP LOCKED behavior, current lease-token ownership, heartbeat renewal, expired-lease recovery, and stale-token rejection.
Worker dispatch must fail closed for unsupported type/version or malformed payload and must preserve safe overlap between old and new worker versions.
Retry, final-attempt exhaustion, dead-letter, repair, and backlog fairness must be bounded by explicit job definitions without inventing payment/provider retry policy.
A portable worker command must run deterministically without starting on app import or defining final worker hosting, autoscaling, process counts, or provider runtime topology.

Operators need source-owned backlog, lease, exhausted-work, worker heartbeat, unsupported-version, and safe event visibility without leaking payloads, identifiers, secrets, or high-cardinality diagnostics.
The durable job foundation must preserve accepted runtime, database, migration, transaction, invariant, SQL-safety, and correlation contracts.

Final worker hosting, provider deployment topology, production worker connection budget, payment/refund/credit/notice handlers, deployed dashboards, alerts, and operational evidence remain later-owned and cannot be closed by provider-independent source tests.
